import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create the catplot to visualize survival rate by sex and passenger class
# kind='bar' automatically calculates the mean of the y-variable for each category
g = sns.catplot(x='sex', y='survived', hue='pclass', data=df, kind='bar', palette='viridis', height=6, aspect=1.2)

# Set the title and axis labels
g.fig.suptitle('Survival Rate by Sex and Passenger Class on the Titanic', y=1.03, fontsize=16)
g.set_axis_labels("Sex", "Survival Rate")

# Improve legend title
g._legend.set_title("Passenger Class")

# Add some padding to the plot
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create the catplot to visualize survival rate by sex and passenger class
# kind='bar' automatically calculates the mean of the y-variable for each category
g = sns.catplot(x='sex', y='survived', hue='pclass', data=df, kind='bar', palette='viridis', height=6, aspect=1.2)

# Set the title and axis labels
g.fig.suptitle('Survival Rate by Sex and Passenger Class on the Titanic', y=1.03, fontsize=16)
g.set_axis_labels("Sex", "Survival Rate")

# Improve legend title
g._legend.set_title("Passenger Class")

# Add some padding to the plot
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
